description: A small Node project with one declared script SURE can turn into a check, and no authorisation to run it. The project is not defective and it is not being asked to be: the case is what a report must do with a check that could not be carried out. The trap is a report that quietly drops it — a reader then sees a headline, a capability line and `No open findings.`, and takes the silence for a pass on the one thing SURE could not do.

read_by.route: the plan holds one entry whose decision is `Denied` (`sure_domain::execution::decide` refused `ActionKind::RunTests` under `InspectOnly`), so `not_run` produces a `CheckResult` whose status is `Skipped` and whose `not_checked_reason` is `NotCheckedReason::ExecutionNotAuthorized`
read_by.returns: one skipped result carrying the frozen sentence, which reaches the reader through `ProjectVerdict::not_checked`, through `Aggregate::coverage.critical_not_checked`, through `CoverageNotCheckedSummary::not_checked` and through the count `render_summary` prints

project.declared_script: "test": "node src/totals.test.js", which is what `npm test` runs
project.dynamic_check: the `test` script becomes one check: `chk_nodetestd6032c00e4d44f94`, titled `run the tests`, severity `must_fix`, critical
project.project_file: `sure.yaml` asks `execution: mode: host_confirmed`. It is a request and not a grant: `Layer::can_grant` refuses a project file, so the run still plans under `inspect_only` and the request is left behind as a refused escalation. The fixture ships it so that a build which read execution authority out of the project would be a red test rather than an undetected escalation.

execution_refusal.why_no_goal: The run supplies no goal, the way `sure check` runs with no `--goal`. That is why the rendered summary carries the after-the-fact caveat as well as the count of checks that could not run; both lines are asserted, so neither can be dropped.

moved.from: not there: the user has granted nothing, so the plan refuses the check
moved.to: one file under a configuration root this test owns, saying `execution: mode: host_confirmed`
moved.how: `Paths::from_roots` puts SURE's configuration root under `target/tmp` for the length of the test, `Authority::load` reads it together with the fixture's own `sure.yaml`, and `Authority::execution()` is the pair `sure check` hands the pipeline. The machine's real configuration directory is never read and never written.

file.why: the whole of what the user's own file says, and the same line `sure check` reads. The file is written rather than a literal being handed to the pipeline, so the route from a person's decision to the run's permissions is the one the product actually has.

moved.keys_are: the two answer blocks compared key by key, sorted. The test reads the difference off the declarations and compares it with this list, so a control that stopped moving something, or started moving something else, is a red test rather than a change nobody noticed.

control.why: The same project, the same `package.json`, the same planned check and the same pipeline run, with the user's own file the only thing that appeared. Standard `sure check` reads execution authority from that file alone, so this is not a test-only route: it is the route. A reporter hard-wired to deny — the failure this fixture exists to catch — would satisfy every positive assertion above and fails here, because the refusal must be gone when the user has granted it.
control.unchanged: The project's own `sure.yaml` still asks for `host_confirmed` in both runs and is still only a request in both: what moves is the user's file. The four keys the two declarations share that say what did *not* move are the summary lines (the same six, line for line), the check's identity and weight, the count of checks that could not run, and the aggregate's headline and severity — the aggregate is `not_enough_checked` either way, because nothing in this build carries a check out. Consent changes what SURE is allowed to do; it does not make anything checked.

required_outcomes.why: The acceptance sentence is *dynamic-not-authorized stays visible*, and every word of it is asserted by equality against SURE's own answer rather than paraphrased. `check_status` is `skipped` and `check_not_checked_reason` is `execution_not_authorized` — the frozen vocabulary has no "not authorized" status at all, so a build that invented one would fail here. `check_reason` is the whole sentence `crates/sure-domain/src/status.rs` fixes for that reason, quoted rather than searched for. Visibility is asserted in four places rather than one, because a struct field is not a report: the result is in `ProjectVerdict::not_checked`, it is in `Aggregate::coverage.critical_not_checked`, it is an entry in `CoverageNotCheckedSummary::not_checked`, and the last line of the rendered summary names it and counts it. `coverage_checked` is zero, which is the honest half a reader could otherwise miss: nothing was checked at all, and the check is neither a pass nor a failure. The project's own `sure.yaml` asking for `host_confirmed` is asserted beside it — `project_ask_refused_escalation` is true, `project_ask_granted` is false — because a build that took execution authority from the project would have made this answer a green light on a stranger's advice.

required_outcomes.why: The fixture is worth nothing without this half, and the assertion that makes it a measurement is the negative one: with the user's own file granting execution, **no result carries `ExecutionNotAuthorized`** — asserted by that predicate, not by a count of passes and not by a greener aggregate. `refusals` is declared as zero and the test computes it as `results().iter().filter(|result| result.not_checked_reason == Some(NotCheckedReason::ExecutionNotAuthorized)).count()`, so a reporter that refused everything fails here and a reporter that refused nothing fails the outcome above. What the check becomes is stated rather than dressed up: `check_status` is `unknown` with `check_reason` *Nothing was reported for this check*, because this build has no runner for a planned check — a check that is no longer refused is still not a check that ran. `coverage_checked` stays zero for that reason, and the aggregate stays `not_enough_checked`, so the honest reading of this half is "the reason changed", not "the project got greener". If a later build learns to carry the check out, this declaration is what has to be re-made, and this sentence is where that decision is written down.

forbidden_outcomes.description: The check that nobody authorised is missing from the report, so the run reads as a project with nothing outstanding. A plan entry that was refused and a plan entry that passed must never look the same to a reader, and `No open findings.` on its own is exactly that mistake.

The project is reported as ready to hand off, as passing, or as verified. The one thing in this project SURE would have had to run to say anything about is the thing it was not allowed to run, so any sentence of that kind is a green light on an unread check.

The lack of authorisation is reported as a defect in the project: a finding, a failure, or a `must_fix` about the code. Nothing here is wrong — the script is declared and the file it names exists — and a project must not be blamed for a permission the person at the keyboard has not given.

The project's own `sure.yaml` is treated as authorisation. A repository SURE was merely pointed at cannot decide that SURE may run it, which is the escalation `docs/architecture/CONFIG_AUTHORITY.md` exists to prevent; a build that read the mode from the project would show this check as allowed.

notes: `dynamic-not-authorized` is a case in `evaluation/acceptance-manifest.json` with `release_blocking: false`, `expected_severity: "note"` and the expectation `unexecuted dynamic checks stay visible as not checked/skipped`; the two fields at the top of this file are copied from that row rather than chosen here, and `every_fixture_agrees_with_the_manifest_about_id_severity_and_blocking` in `crates/sure-testkit/tests/fixture_apps.rs` fails if either drifts. The row is why this fixture is **not** in `FIXTURES_WITHOUT_A_MANIFEST_CASE`: it has a case, and the exemption list is checked in both directions. SURE reports no `Finding` for this case — a `note` is a ceiling this fixture stays far under — and the `must_fix` the check itself carries is the weight of the check, not a candidate about the project: `candidates.material` and `candidates.style_noise` are both empty, which the test asserts rather than leaves to a reader. This is the second fixture in the corpus that ships a `package.json` without being one of `P14-T001`'s scanners, so it is named in `TYPESCRIPT_FIXTURES` for the reason that file gives — a directory that ships a `package.json` is a Node application and belongs in the runnability sweep — and the test that grades it lives in `crates/sure-core/tests/adversarial_fixture_detection.rs`, where the real pipeline is reachable. The pipeline is driven with `store: None`, so grading this fixture writes nothing anywhere, and the project is read where it ships rather than copied, so a fixture edited without the test being edited is a red test.
